# VTLabs IoT Training Kit - Example Curriculum

<!-- GENERATED by tools/make_catalogue.py from the example headers - do not edit -->

64 examples. In the Arduino IDE: select the VTLabs board, then **File > Examples > VTLabsKit** (under 'Examples for VTLabs IoT Training Kit').

Every sketch's header lists purpose, hardware/wiring, libraries, expected behaviour, experiments and troubleshooting. Add-on lessons need the matching **Tools > Keypad / LED Matrix** setting; without it they stop with a clear message.

Learning outcomes: [learning-outcomes.md](learning-outcomes.md). Libraries: [libraries.md](libraries.md).

## Level 1 - Digital input and output

| Example | Purpose | Hardware | Libraries |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L1_01 Blink**<br>`L1_01_Blink` | Check that board, driver and upload work. | base kit | none |
| **L1_02 Read a Push Button**<br>`L1_02_ButtonRead` | Read a digital input with digitalRead() and understand "active LOW" buttons with pull-up resistors. | base kit | none |
| **L1_03 Button Controls an LED**<br>`L1_03_ButtonControlsLED` | Combine an input and an output: hold-to-light, then toggle. | base kit | none |
| **L1_04 Read a Switch (operating mode)**<br>`L1_04_SwitchRead` | A switch keeps its position - use it to select a mode. | base kit | none |
| **L1_05 Debouncing**<br>`L1_05_Debounce` | Mechanical contacts bounce for a few milliseconds. | base kit | none |
| **L1_06 Digital Sensor: PIR Motion**<br>`L1_06_PIRMotion` | Read a sensor that gives a digital (HIGH/LOW) output. | base kit | none |
| **L1_07 Buzzer and Relay - Safely**<br>`L1_07_BuzzerRelaySafe` | Drive actuators through their transistor drivers, with a known safe state at start-up and an automatic switch-off. | base kit | none |
| **L1_08 Traffic Light State Machine**<br>`L1_08_TrafficLight` | Program a sequence as a state machine with millis(), so the board can still react to a pedestrian button. | base kit | none |

## Level 2 - Analog input, PWM and DAC

| Example | Purpose | Hardware | Libraries |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L2_01 Read a Potentiometer (ADC)**<br>`L2_01_Potentiometer` | Convert a voltage into a number with analogRead(). | base kit | none |
| **L2_02 Light Sensor (LDR)**<br>`L2_02_LDR` | Read a light-dependent resistor through a voltage divider. | base kit | none |
| **L2_03 From Raw ADC Counts to Engineering Units**<br>`L2_03_CalibratedUnits` | Turn raw readings into meaningful units: - POT: millivolts using the ESP32's factory calibration (analogReadMilliVolts) compared with the naive formula. | base kit | none |
| **L2_04 Filtering Noisy Readings**<br>`L2_04_Filtering` | Compare raw readings with a moving average and an exponential moving average (EMA) on the Serial Plotter. | base kit | none |
| **L2_05 Dim an LED with PWM**<br>`L2_05_PWMFade` | Pulse-width modulation: switch fast, vary the ON time. | base kit | none |
| **L2_06 ADC vs PWM vs true DAC**<br>`L2_06_ADC_PWM_DAC` | The potentiometer (ADC input) sets two outputs at once: - LED_YELLOW by PWM  (pin switches 0 V / 3.3 V very fast) - LED_GREEN  by DAC2 (pin outputs a real steady voltage) | base kit | none |
| **L2_07 Potentiometer Dimmer**<br>`L2_07_PotDimmer` | Map an input range to an output range with map() and constrain(); add a dead band so the LED is fully off at the end. | base kit | none |
| **L2_08 Tones and a Melody**<br>`L2_08_BuzzerMelody` | A passive buzzer plays the frequency you send with tone(). | base kit | none |

## Level 3 - Serial communication: UART, I2C, SPI, RS485

| Example | Purpose | Hardware | Libraries |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L3_01 Diagnostics over USB Serial**<br>`L3_01_SerialDiagnostics` | Use Serial as a debugging tool: board report, formatted values, timing, and the ESP32 log levels. | base kit | none |
| **L3_02 Exchanging Data Between Two UART Devices**<br>`L3_02_UART2Exchange` | Use the second hardware UART (Serial2) to talk to another device. | base kit | none |
| **L3_03 Serial Command Parser**<br>`L3_03_SerialCommandParser` | Control the kit by typing commands: read a line, split it into words, validate, act, and answer OK/ERROR. | base kit | none |
| **L3_04 I2C Address Scanner**<br>`L3_04_I2CScanner` | Find every device on the I2C bus and name the ones the kit knows about. | base kit | none |
| **L3_05 Temperature and Humidity (DHT22)**<br>`L3_05_DHT22` | Read a sensor that uses its own single-wire digital protocol, and handle failed readings properly. | base kit | "DHT sensor library" by Adafruit (>= 1.4.6) + "Adafruit Unified Sensor" (installed automatically with it) |
| **L3_06 I2C Sensor: BME280 (OPTIONAL MODULE)**<br>`L3_06_I2CSensorBME280` | Talk to a sensor over I2C: address, init check, readings. | base kit | "Adafruit BME280 Library" (>= 2.2) + "Adafruit Unified Sensor" + "Adafruit BusIO" |
| **L3_07 Show Measurements on the OLED Display**<br>`L3_07_OLEDMeasurements` | Draw text and a bar graph on an I2C OLED (SSD1306). | base kit | "Adafruit SSD1306" (>= 2.5) + "Adafruit GFX Library" + "Adafruit BusIO" "DHT sensor library" + "Adafruit Unified Sensor" |
| **L3_08 SPI Peripheral: micro-SD Card (OPTIONAL MODULE)**<br>`L3_08_SPISDCard` | Use the SPI bus (SCK, MOSI, MISO + one chip-select per device) to write and read a file. | base kit | none |
| **L3_09 Introduction to RS485 (OPTIONAL MODULE)**<br>`L3_09_RS485` | RS485 sends UART data as a differential pair (A/B) - up to ~1200 m and many devices on one cable. | base kit | none |

## Level 4 - IoT networking

| Example | Purpose | Hardware | Libraries |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L4_01 Connect to Wi-Fi**<br>`L4_01_WiFiConnect` | Join a Wi-Fi network as a station, with a timeout, status LED, signal strength and automatic reconnection. | base kit | none |
| **L4_02 Host a Local Web Server**<br>`L4_02_WebServerHello` | Serve web pages from the ESP32: routes, HTTP status codes, query parameters. | base kit | none |
| **L4_03 Sensor Dashboard in the Browser**<br>`L4_03_WebDashboard` | Separate data (JSON API) from presentation (HTML + JavaScript). | base kit | "DHT sensor library" + "Adafruit Unified Sensor" |
| **L4_04 Control an Output from a Web Page - Safely**<br>`L4_04_WebControlOutput` | Switch LEDs and the relay from a browser, with safety rules: only POST requests change outputs, the relay has a maximum ON time, and a local button always overrides the web. | base kit | none |
| **L4_05 Log Measurements to Flash (LittleFS)**<br>`L4_05_LogMeasurements` | Store measurements in the ESP32's own flash file system and download them as a CSV file from the browser. | base kit | "DHT sensor library" + "Adafruit Unified Sensor" (LittleFS is in the core) |
| **L4_06 MQTT: Publish and Subscribe (advanced)**<br>`L4_06_MQTTPublish` | Send sensor data to an MQTT broker and receive commands. | base kit | "PubSubClient" by Nick O'Leary (>= 2.8), "DHT sensor library" + "Adafruit Unified Sensor" |

## Level 5 - Integrated projects

| Example | Purpose | Hardware | Libraries |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L5_01 Project: Automatic Lighting**<br>`L5_01_AutomaticLighting` | Combine sensors, decisions and an actuator: the "lamp" (LED_YELLOW, PWM) turns on when it is dark AND someone is present, fades smoothly, and stays on for a while. | base kit | none |
| **L5_02 Project: Temperature-Based Fan Control**<br>`L5_02_TemperatureFanControl` | Two control methods side by side: 1) ON/OFF with hysteresis -> RELAY (fan on/off) 2) Proportional -> LED_RED brightness = simulated fan speed (PWM) | base kit | "DHT sensor library" + "Adafruit Unified Sensor" |
| **L5_03 Project: Environmental Monitor (offline)**<br>`L5_03_EnvironmentalMonitor` | A stand-alone monitor: several sensors, min/max statistics, display pages, and alarm indication with LEDs. | base kit | "Adafruit SSD1306" + "Adafruit GFX Library" + "Adafruit BusIO", "DHT sensor library" + "Adafruit Unified Sensor" |
| **L5_04 Project: Time-Stamped Data Logger**<br>`L5_04_DataLogger` | A complete logger: real date/time from the internet (NTP), CSV in flash, start/stop with a button, status on the OLED, download over Wi-Fi. | base kit | "Adafruit SSD1306" + "Adafruit GFX Library" + "Adafruit BusIO", "DHT sensor library" + "Adafruit Unified Sensor" |
| **L5_05 Project: Local Wi-Fi Control (no router)**<br>`L5_05_LocalWiFiControl` | The kit creates its OWN Wi-Fi network (access point). | base kit | none |
| **L5_06 Project: Complete Sensor-to-Dashboard System**<br>`L5_06_SensorToDashboard` | End-to-end IoT system on one board: sensors -> filtering -> history buffer -> JSON API -> web dashboard with a live chart (drawn with plain JavaScript, works without internet) -> alarm -> local indicators. | base kit | "DHT sensor library" + "Adafruit Unified Sensor" |

## Level 6 - Matrix keypad

| Example | Purpose | Hardware | Libraries |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L6_01 How a Matrix Keypad is Scanned**<br>`L6_01_KeypadRawScan` | A 4x4 keypad has 16 keys but only 8 wires: 4 rows x 4 columns. | Keypad add-on | none |
| **L6_02 Read Individual Keys**<br>`L6_02_KeypadReadKeys` | Use the VTLKeypad class: one call returns the key that was just pressed - scanning and debouncing are done for you. | Keypad add-on | none |
| **L6_03 Debouncing, Hold and Release Events**<br>`L6_03_KeypadEvents` | Real keys bounce. | Keypad add-on | none |
| **L6_04 Numeric Input with Validation**<br>`L6_04_NumericInput` | Type a number on the keypad, edit it, confirm it, and check that it is within the allowed range. | Keypad add-on | none |
| **L6_05 Password (PIN) Entry**<br>`L6_05_PasswordEntry` | Enter a hidden PIN, compare it, limit wrong attempts with a lock-out timer, and change the PIN (stored in flash). | Keypad add-on | none |
| **L6_06 Menu Navigation on the OLED**<br>`L6_06_MenuNavigation` | Build a menu system: a list, a cursor, enter and back. | Keypad add-on | "Adafruit SSD1306" + "Adafruit GFX Library" + "Adafruit BusIO", "DHT sensor library" + "Adafruit Unified Sensor" |
| **L6_07 Configurable System Settings**<br>`L6_07_ConfigurableSettings` | Let the user change settings with the keypad, validate them, and keep them in flash (Preferences) so they survive a reset. | Keypad add-on | "Adafruit SSD1306" + "Adafruit GFX Library" + "Adafruit BusIO" (Preferences is part of the ESP32 core) |
| **L6_08 Keypad as the Kit's Control Panel**<br>`L6_08_KeypadControlsKit` | Combine keypad input with LEDs, sensors, display and actuators. | Keypad add-on | "Adafruit SSD1306" + "Adafruit GFX Library" + "Adafruit BusIO", "DHT sensor library" + "Adafruit Unified Sensor" |

| Example | Purpose | Hardware | Libraries |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L7_01 MAX7219 LED Matrix: Pixels and Rows**<br>`L7_01_MAX7219_Pixels` | Learn how the MAX7219 driver works, using its own library. | MAX7219 matrix | "MD_MAX72XX" by majicDesigns (>= 3.5) |

| **L7_04 WS2812: Brightness, Power and Gamma**<br>`L7_04_WS2812_BrightnessPower` | Each WS2812 draws up to ~60 mA at full white (20 mA per colour). | WS2812 matrix | "Adafruit NeoPixel" (>= 1.12) |

## Level 8 - LED matrix, portable API

| Example | Purpose | Hardware | Libraries |
|---|---|---|---|
| **L8_01 Individual Pixel Control (any matrix)**<br>`L8_01_MatrixPixels` | Control single LEDs by (x, y) with the VTLMatrix API, which works the same on MAX7219 and WS2812 modules. | LED matrix (any) | MAX7219: "MD_MAX72XX" + "MD_Parola" WS2812:  "Adafruit NeoPixel" + "Adafruit NeoMatrix" + "Adafruit GFX Library" |
| **L8_02 Numbers and Symbols (any matrix)**<br>`L8_02_MatrixNumbersSymbols` | Show numbers with a tiny 3x5 font (two digits fit on 8x8) and 8x8 symbols (icons stored as 8 bytes, one per row). | LED matrix (any) | as L8_01 |

| **L8_04 Scrolling Text (any matrix)**<br>`L8_04_MatrixScrollText` | Scroll text WITHOUT blocking the program: scrollText() starts, scrollUpdate() moves one step when it is time and returns true when the text has left the display. | LED matrix (any) | as L8_01 |
| **L8_05 Animations (any matrix)**<br>`L8_05_MatrixAnimations` | An animation is a sequence of frames drawn at a steady rate. | LED matrix (any) | as L8_01 |
| **L8_06 Showing Sensor Measurements (any matrix)**<br>`L8_06_MatrixSensorValue` | Present a measurement three ways and choose the right one: number (exact), bar graph (quick to read), scrolling text with units (full information). | LED matrix (any) | as L8_01, plus "DHT sensor library" + "Adafruit Unified Sensor" |
| **L8_07 System Status and Warnings (any matrix)**<br>`L8_07_MatrixStatusWarnings` | Use the matrix as a status panel: one icon per state, blinking for urgency, priority when several problems happen at once. | LED matrix (any) | as L8_01, plus "DHT sensor library" + "Adafruit Unified Sensor" SENSOR FAULT  cross, fast blink       (DHT22 read failed) OVER-TEMP     warning, blink + beep   (T above POT-set limit 20..40 C) DARK          arrow down              (light < 10 %) MOTION        bell                    (PIR active) OK            check, steady |

| **L9_03 Exercise 3: Access-Control Demonstration**<br>`L9_03_AccessControl` | A door-lock simulation: PIN entry, status indicators, an actuator with automatic re-lock, and an event log. | Keypad add-on (optional: LED matrix (any)) | none |
